comments.body:
## RCA — confirmed root cause (Phase 1 complete)

### Mechanism

`material_basis()` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/material_diff.py:65-86`) is the single source
of the mapping the composite fingerprint hashes. It passes the description through exactly
one canonicalization — `normalize_checkbox_state()`
(`material_diff.py:58-62`) — and nothing else:

    "description": normalize_checkbox_state(ctx.description)
    if normalize_checkboxes
    else ctx.description,

`pass1.material_fingerprint()` (`pass1.py:739-757`) then hashes that basis. Because no
whitespace canonicalization exists anywhere on that path, **every** insignificant-whitespace
variant of the same description produces a different composite hash, and the gate reports
`stale-material`.

### Runtime proof (fingerprints over a fixed PlanContext, current `main`)

    SAME    baseline
    DIFFER  trailing newline stripped        <- the reported repro
    DIFFER  extra trailing newline
    DIFFER  trailing space on a line
    DIFFER  CRLF line endings
    DIFFER  leading blank line
    SAME    -- checkbox ticked (control)
    DIFFER  -- WORD CHANGED (must differ)
    DIFFER  -- INDENT CHANGED (nesting)

The checkbox control confirms the 330c precedent is live and working on the same path, which
discriminates "no canonicalization at all" from "canonicalization exists but misses
whitespace": the mechanism is specifically the *absence* of a whitespace pass, not a broken
normalizer.

### Legitimacy: defect

The cited design invariant is that content which carries no plan substance is normalized out
before hashing — `material_diff.py:58-62` ("Box state is progress metadata ... so it must not
stale a signed review (bug 330c)") and `docs/plan-review-gate.md:471-475`. The gate also
contradicts its own required workflow: the close precheck *requires* editing the description
to tick every AC box, and the documented CLI path for that (`--description="$(cat file)"`)
strips the trailing newline as a shell artifact.

### Fix shape — reuse the 330c precedent, do not invent a parallel mechanism

Add a sibling of `normalize_checkbox_state` in the same module, applied at the same single
point in `material_basis`, under the same flag.

**Security property preserved.** The canonicalization is provably whitespace-ONLY:

- line endings normalized (CRLF/CR -> LF)
- trailing whitespace stripped **per line**
- leading/trailing blank lines at the document boundary stripped

**Leading whitespace is deliberately preserved** — indentation changes markdown list nesting,
which is structural, and the `INDENT CHANGED` control above must keep differing. Interior
blank lines are preserved — they separate paragraphs. No character other than whitespace is
touched, and no whitespace *between* non-whitespace characters is touched, so no edit that
changes any word, any ordering, or any nesting can be collapsed.

### Back-compat

`normalize_checkboxes=False` (the pre-330c legacy algorithm used by
`attest._legacy_material_ok`, `attest.py:645-660`) keeps hashing the **raw** description, so
the 96d1 grandfather still reproduces the pre-330c algorithm byte-exactly.

### Caller-dependency sweep

The only behavioural dependant of the current byte-exact hashing is that legacy path, which
is preserved by construction. Every other caller (`material_components`,
`relation_snapshot.current_material_fingerprint_impl`, the gates) compares a computed hash to
a computed hash and is indifferent to the basis contents.

comments.body:
## Resolved — Gerrit change 1501, MERGED

https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1501 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, submitted)

**Proven root cause.** `material_basis()`
(`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/material_diff.py`) is the single source of the mapping the
composite fingerprint hashes, and it applied exactly one canonicalization to the description
— `normalize_checkbox_state()` — and nothing else. With no whitespace pass anywhere on that
path, every insignificant-whitespace variant hashed differently. The checkbox control
fingerprinting SAME on the same run discriminated "no canonicalization at all" from "a broken
normalizer": the mechanism is specifically the absence of a whitespace pass.

**Fix — the 330c precedent extended, not a parallel mechanism.**
`normalize_insignificant_whitespace()` was added as a sibling of `normalize_checkbox_state()`
in the same module and applied at the same single point in `material_basis`, via a
`canonical_description()` helper that keeps both canonicalizations in one place.

**The security property, and how it is proven.** The canonicalization touches only:
line-ending form (CRLF/CR -> LF), whitespace at the END of a line, and blank lines at the
DOCUMENT boundary. It never touches leading whitespace, never touches whitespace between two
non-whitespace characters, and never removes an interior blank line. Eight negative controls
pin that it did not widen too far — all must still read `stale-material`:

    a word changed  |  a sentence appended  |  an AC item's text changed
    an AC item removed  |  indent ADDED to a list item  |  indent REMOVED from a list item
    interior blank line removed (paragraphs joined)  |  interior space removed (words joined)

Leading indentation is deliberately material: it restructures markdown list nesting.

**Test:** `tests/unit/plan_review/test_2be7_whitespace_material.py`. Confirmed legitimately
RED first (9 failures, including the gate test reproducing this ticket's exact
`stale-material` verdict), and held out from the subagent that wrote the fix — it never saw
the file. Mutation check: making the whitespace normalizer a no-op returns all 9 to RED, so
the pass is not vacuous. Coverage is at both tiers — the fingerprint itself, and
`attest.compute_validity`, which is the single dispatcher the claim gate and the close gate
both read through, so a `certified` verdict there is what `review-plan --status` reports.

**Back-compat repair the investigation surfaced.** Landing the canonicalization broke
`test_94a3_material_diff.py::test_pre330c_attestation_over_unticked_boxes_survives_ticking`
— a genuine regression of bug 94a3, not a stale expectation. `_legacy_material_ok` now tries
BOTH superseded generations (pre-330c raw, and post-330c/pre-2be7 checkbox-only). This opens
no staleness hole: each candidate is a full hash comparison against the CURRENT material, so
a real edit matches none. `normalize_checkboxes=False` still reproduces the pre-330c
algorithm byte-exactly, and `test_legacy_material_grandfather_96d1.py` passes untouched.

**Regression:** full unit suite 8785 passed / 28 skipped / 0 failed locally; lint and
typecheck clean; CI green on py3.12, py3.13 and macOS. (The first CI attempt's py3.11 leg was
cancelled at the 60-minute job limit — a timeout, not a failure; `recheck` came back green.)

**Parity sweep — one gap found and dispositioned:** 8aed-f307-8faa-49c6 (linked
`discovered_from`). `no_file_impact_reason` is the basis's other free-text field and is still
hashed raw. Deliberately left out of scope: it is a short single-line string not subject to
the `$(cat file)` newline-stripping repro, and widening the canonicalized surface without its
own RED test is exactly the over-collapse this ticket warned against.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Whitespace-only edits do not change the material fingerprint; a signed review stays
      certified.
- [x] The close gate does not report `stale-material` for a whitespace-only edit.
- [x] A regression test drives sign -> trailing-newline-only edit -> still certified.
- [x] Semantically meaningful edits still invalidate (eight negative controls).

compiled_state.description:
## Summary
Whitespace-only changes to a ticket description invalidate its signed plan-review attestation, forcing an unnecessary (slow, costly) re-review before the close gate will accept the ticket.

## Repro (observed this session on 28cd-d8f8-4456-482c)
1. A ticket has a certified/signed plan review at description length 7098 chars (ending in a single trailing newline).
2. Re-set the description via `rebar edit --description="$(cat file)"` — shell command substitution strips the trailing newline, so the stored description becomes 7097 chars. The visible content is byte-identical apart from that one trailing \n.
3. `rebar review-plan <id> --status` returns `{"ok": false, "verdict": "stale-material", "reason": "the plan was materially edited since review — changed: description (7098 -> 7097 chars)"}`.
4. `rebar transition <id> in_progress closed` is blocked by the plan-review close gate with 'stale-material' and demands a fresh `review-plan`.

Note (contrast): ticking acceptance-criteria checkboxes (`- [ ]` -> `- [x]`) is correctly hash-invisible and does NOT invalidate the review. Only the insignificant-whitespace delta (a trailing newline) drifted the material fingerprint.

## Expected
Plan-review material canonicalization should normalize insignificant whitespace before hashing so that whitespace-only edits — trailing/leading newline differences, trailing spaces on a line, and analogous no-semantic-change edits — do not invalidate a signed plan review or trip the stale-material close gate. Only semantically meaningful description changes should drift the material.

## Impact
An operator ticking ACs and re-saving a description (a routine close-time step, and one where CLI $(...) newline-stripping is easy to hit) can be forced into a full LLM re-review (~7-15 min + model spend) purely for a trailing-newline difference. This wastes gate budget and slows the close path, and risks tempting a --force bypass.

## Suggested fix direction
In the plan-review material builder (the description material-part hash, currently reported like 'description <hash> <char-count>'), apply a canonicalization pass (e.g. strip trailing whitespace per line + normalize trailing newlines to a single canonical form, consistent with how AC-checkbox state is already normalized out) before fingerprinting. Add a regression test asserting that a trailing-newline-only edit keeps review-plan --status 'certified'.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Adding or removing a trailing newline (or trailing whitespace on lines) in a ticket description does not change the plan-review material fingerprint, so a previously signed review stays 'certified' per `rebar review-plan <id> --status`.
- [x] The plan-review close gate does not report 'stale-material' for a whitespace-only description edit.
- [x] A regression test drives: sign a review, apply a trailing-newline-only description edit, assert `review-plan --status` stays certified and the close gate is not blocked on stale-material.
- [x] Semantically meaningful description edits still correctly invalidate the review (the normalization does not over-collapse real changes).
compiled_state.title: Whitespace-only description edits must not invalidate plan-review material
